facts.text: Staged intervention means escalating from information to warning, slowing, partial braking and maximum safe braking, and refusing motion for a stationary machine, rather than jumping directly to a full stop.
facts.quote: Staged intervention means the system escalates step by step, from information to warning to slowing to partial braking to maximum safe braking and, for a stationary machine, to refusing to move, rather than jumping straight to a full stop.

facts.text: Staged intervention gives the operator a chance to act before the machine intervenes and reserves harsh actions for situations that need them.
facts.quote: Staging gives the operator a chance to act before the machine acts, and it saves the harsh actions for the moments that need them.

facts.text: The booklet's earth-moving-machine intervention ladder uses a visual or spatial information indication when an object is present and the stopping margin is healthy.
facts.quote: Information: an object is present and the stopping margin is healthy; a visual or spatial indication.

facts.text: The booklet's earth-moving-machine intervention ladder uses an urgent warning—a distinct sound, light or haptic cue—when risk is rising but the operator still has adequate margin.
facts.quote: Urgent warning: risk is rising while the operator still has adequate margin; a distinct sound, light or haptic cue.

facts.text: The booklet's earth-moving-machine intervention ladder applies automatic slowing when the operator has not reduced the risk, by reducing propel, using the retarder or hydrostatic slowing, or applying light braking.
facts.quote: Automatic slowing: the operator has not reduced the risk; reduce propel, use the retarder or hydrostatic slowing, or apply light braking.

facts.text: The booklet's earth-moving-machine intervention ladder applies partial service braking when the margin approaches its minimum, using controlled deceleration below stability and traction limits.
facts.quote: Partial service braking: margin approaching its minimum; controlled deceleration below stability and traction limits.

facts.text: The booklet's earth-moving-machine intervention ladder applies maximum safe collision-mitigation braking when collision is otherwise unavoidable, using the hardest braking allowed by current stability and control limits.
facts.quote: Maximum safe collision-mitigation braking: collision otherwise unavoidable; the hardest braking the current stability and control limits allow.

facts.text: The booklet's earth-moving-machine intervention ladder uses stopped-state hold to keep the brake on when speed is zero and the hazard remains.
facts.quote: Stopped-state hold: speed zero while the hazard remains; keep the brake on.

facts.text: The booklet's earth-moving-machine intervention ladder inhibits motion from standstill by rejecting or limiting the propel or articulation command when an object is already in the projected path before the machine moves.
facts.quote: Motion inhibit from standstill: an object is already in the projected path before the machine moves; reject or limit the propel or articulation command.

facts.text: The booklet's state diagram uses the compact state names UrgentWarning, Slowing, PartialBraking, MaximumSafeBraking, Hold and MotionInhibit, in the style of the ISO 21815 standards.
facts.quote: The booklet's state diagram writes these as compact names, UrgentWarning, Slowing, PartialBraking, MaximumSafeBraking, Hold and MotionInhibit, in the style of the ISO 21815 standards.

facts.text: The ISO 21815 standards describe speed reduction, stopping and motion inhibit.
facts.quote: The standards themselves speak of speed reduction, stopping and motion inhibit

facts.text: ISO/TS 21815-2 defines network commands to slow down, stop or prevent motion of the machine.
facts.quote: ISO/TS 21815-2 defines the network commands to "slow down, stop or prevent motion of the machine"

facts.text: EMESRT (Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table) places awareness at Level 7, advisory controls at Level 8, and intervention controls that slow and stop the vehicle at Level 9.
facts.quote: The industry body EMESRT (Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table) places awareness at Level 7, advisory controls at Level 8 and intervention controls that slow and stop the vehicle at Level 9

entities.name: Earth Moving Equipment Safety Round Table

facts.text: South African law prescribes the intervention sequence detect, warn, retard to a safe speed, then brake.
facts.quote: South African law prescribes the sequence detect, warn, retard to a safe speed, then brake [Chapter 3].

facts.text: Road systems stage interventions as warning, a brief haptic brake jerk, partial braking and full braking.
facts.quote: Road systems stage warning, a brief haptic brake jerk, partial braking and full braking [Chapter 8].

facts.text: Staging makes automatic braking acceptable to people working around the machine; mine leaders preferred an integration that slowed to a crawl before setting the brake rather than an abrupt stop.
facts.quote: Staging is what makes an automatic brake acceptable to the people who work around it: mine leaders preferred an integration that slowed to a crawl before setting the brake, "not an abrupt stop" [Chapter 4].

facts.text: Each intervention stage needs its own acceptance tolerance because an unnecessary advisory differs from an unnecessary emergency stop of a loaded machine.
facts.quote: Each stage needs its own acceptance tolerance, because an unnecessary advisory is not the same as an unnecessary emergency stop of a loaded machine [Chapter 3].
